equity_bridge.note: Q2 2026 10-Q balance sheet, 2026-06-30; the matching interest income is excluded from the flows

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (6.7-6.9%) differs >30% from revenue 3yr CAGR (2.8%) and EPS 3yr CAGR (1.1%). Book value is not the right growth anchor here: equity growth reflects retained earnings net of ~$1-1.6B/yr buybacks and acquisitions, while the operating business grew revenue ~3% organically FY22-25. Revenue 5yr CAGR (4.9%, includes Belcan M&A) is used as the reference and the base path sits below it after FY2026.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - ~$50M/yr equity-award taxes - interest income): FY2020 $2,500M, FY2022 $1,866M, FY2025 $2,259M. The 5yr figure is negative because FY2020 was flattered by COVID-era payroll-tax deferrals and a receivables release. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR exceeds reported because SBC fell from $261M (FY2022) to $181M (FY2025) -- SBC is shrinking relative to cash flow, the opposite of the dilution warning. EPS 5yr CAGR starts from a depressed FY2020 ($2.58); FY2025 GAAP EPS $4.57 carries the $0.80 non-cash OBBBA charge.

scenario_narratives.base: Cognizant delivers FY2026 on guidance (revenue ~+5% including 3Cloud and Astreya, adjusted operating margin ~16.1%) and then grows organically at 3-4%, fading to 2.5% -- roughly its FY22-25 organic pace. The two axes that matter, AI-driven productivity deflation of legacy application-development/maintenance hours versus new AI-transformation and managed-services demand, roughly cancel; Project Leap's $230-320M of 2026 cash charges fund the 'broader and shorter pyramid' and margins hold near 16% adjusted. Cash tax stays ~27.5% of EBIT, above the book rate, as it has for three years.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Q2 2026 pattern persists: seven $100M+ TCV wins a quarter, Financial Services growing double digits, Health Sciences steady on the TriZetto platform, and 3Cloud (Azure/AI) and Astreya (AI infrastructure managed services) give Cognizant a credible AI-builder position. Organic growth runs 5-6.5% for three years before fading, and the AI-enabled delivery model lets revenue per head rise while the pyramid shrinks, adding ~1.5pp to adjusted operating margin (toward 17.5-18%, still below Accenture's).
scenario_narratives.bear: The market's fear case, and why the stock sits near the bottom of its 37-87 range: agentic coding and testing tools collapse the effort in application maintenance and testing, historically Cognizant's core, clients reprice renewals, and the commoditised remainder is fought over by the lower-cost Indian majors. Revenue flattens in FY2027 and shrinks 1.5% in each of FY2028-29 before stabilising at 1-1.5% growth, adjusted operating margin compresses ~2.5pp, the CMT segment keeps shrinking, and US visa policy and the India-Mauritius treaty change raise cost and cash tax. It is a shrinking business rather than a cash-burning one, so the terminal value is capped at 10x rather than floored at zero.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A mature, cash-generative IT services company priced at roughly 10x adjusted earnings and ~11-12x owner FCF because the market is pricing a meaningful chance that GenAI hollows out its labour-based revenue model. The owner-FCF build charges SBC, Project Leap cash and a cash tax rate above the book rate, and grows only organically after FY2026 so acquired growth is never valued without its purchase price. The valuation turns on one question -- whether AI is net deflationary for Cognizant's revenue -- which is why the bear case is heavily weighted and the terminal multiple is capped at 14x base / 10x bear.
key_risks_to_valuation: GenAI/agentic tooling deflating application development, maintenance and testing revenue faster than AI-services demand replaces it
Pricing pressure from TCS, Infosys, HCLTech and Accenture compressing the ~16% adjusted operating margin
Cash tax rate persistently above the book rate (India payments, foreign R&E capitalisation, India-Mauritius treaty amendment)
India ITD dispute over the 2016 CTS India buyback -- contingent liability and deposit are both excluded from the equity bridge
Debt-funded buybacks and acquisitions ($1B revolver drawn Q2 2026) turned net cash into net debt; continued M&A at high prices would destroy value the organic-only model does not capture
US H-1B visa fee/cap changes raising onshore delivery costs

inputs.share_count_basis: 452M Class A shares issued and outstanding at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 10-Q balance sheet) plus ~1M dilutive SBC shares (Q2 10-Q EPS note: six-month dilutive effect 1M). May-2026 $500M ASR reported as completed (9.7M shares). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; buybacks are the cash mechanism that keeps it flat.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back $181M (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation) plus ~$50M estimated cash tax withheld on net-share settlement. Cognizant publishes no combined figure and does not tag the withholding; it sits inside 'Repurchases of common stock'. Estimate from disclosed quarters: Q4-2025 $13M (FY2025 10-K Item 5), Q2-2026 $10M (Q2 2026 10-Q Item 2), annualised with a heavier Q1 vesting quarter.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. US 10y ~4.3% + beta ~1.0 x 5.0% ERP = ~9.3% cost of equity; debt is ~6% of EV (revolver + term loan at SOFR+spread, ~4% after tax) -> WACC ~9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: the AI-deflation risk is carried in the bear driver path and its 25% weight, not stacked as a rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating lease cost ($~200M/yr) is a single straight-line charge inside operating expense, so it is already inside EBITDA/EBIT. Operating lease liabilities ($534M at 2026-06-30) are NOT in net debt. One treatment, charged once. Finance leases immaterial (10-K Note 6).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row 1 -- US-listed operating company, IT services; USD filings/USD quote, US GAAP, SBC expensed, no NCI, so owner-fcf-adaptations.md not needed). First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY entry, no prior DCF). ANCHORS: revenue base FY2025 $21,108M (10-K). Net debt from the Q2 2026 10-Q balance sheet (2026-06-30), the latest filing and later than the DB's Q1 2026 row: cash $1,038M + short-term investments $13M = $1,051M; debt = revolver $1,000M (drawn Q2 2026 to fund the $1.15B Q2 buyback and the $634M Astreya purchase) + Term Loan $561M ($33M current + $527M long-term, net of $1M fees) = $1,560M. Net debt $509M. The company went from ~$1.4B net cash at FY2025 to net debt within six months: $1.6B of H1 buybacks + $1.33B of acquisitions (3Cloud Jan-26, Astreya Q2-26). Long-term investments ($106M) added in the equity bridge. INTEREST INCOME: $105M FY2025 is deducted from last_fcf for consistency with the forward component build, which starts from EBITDA and therefore excludes it; the cash now earns less (Q2-26 interest income $18M vs $23M) and the company is net-indebted, so there is no double count going forward either way. BUYBACKS: a heavy repurchaser ($1,378M FY2025, $1,607M H1 2026; count 479M -> 452M in six months), so the flat count is funded many times over, not a convention. FY2026 GUIDANCE (Q2 call, 29-Jul-2026): revenue +4.0-6.5% cc incl. 3Cloud/Astreya; adjusted operating margin ~16.0-16.2%; adj EPS $5.70-5.82; Q3 revenue $5.60-5.68B. Project Leap restructuring $230-320M (substantially all cash, 2026) is excluded from adjusted margin but is real cash, so it is charged in the FY2026 EBITDA margin (~1.2pp). The $81M Q2 India DC-obligation reversal is non-cash and ignored. TAX: FY2025 GAAP ETR distorted by a one-time non-cash $390M OBBBA DTA write-off (Q3 2025); FY2024 ETR 24.1%. But CASH taxes have run well above the book rate: $985M on $3,488M pretax in FY2025 (28%) even after a ~$200M OBBBA saving, $1,120M on $2,953M in FY2024 -- foreign R&E capitalisation remains and India cash payments are heavy. Base cash tax on EBIT 27.5%. Reconciliation of the build to FY2025: at FY2025 components the build gives ~$2.46B unlevered owner FCF vs $2.36B actual (reported $2,595M - SBC incl. taxes $231M), within ~4%; a recurring ~0.5pp restructuring haircut from FY2027 closes that gap (see assumptions.base.ebitda_margin_rationale). M&A: revenue growth beyond FY2026 is modelled ORGANIC only, because acquisition spend is not in owner FCF; FY2026 includes 3Cloud/Astreya revenue whose purchase price is already out of the 2026-06-30 cash balance. RISK not in the bridge: the long-running India ITD dispute over the 2016 CTS India share buyback (deposits held in other noncurrent assets) -- neither the deposit nor the contingent liability is added.

bear.narrative: GenAI coding and testing agents deflate the billable-hours base faster than AI services replace it: revenue shrinks in FY2028-29 as application-maintenance renewals reprice 20-30% lower, pricing pressure from TCS/Infosys/HCLTech compresses adjusted operating margin ~2.5pp, and H-1B cost/visa tightening plus the India-Mauritius treaty amendment push the cash tax rate higher.

base.narrative: FY2026 on guidance (~5% reported incl. acquisitions; adj op margin ~16.1% = ~19.7% pre-SBC EBITDA, less ~1.2pp of Project Leap cash). Organic growth then 3-4% fading to 2.5%, margin flat at ~16.2% adjusted operating (less ~0.5pp of recurring restructuring cash): AI productivity savings and pyramid reshaping roughly offset AI pricing deflation.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA = adjusted operating margin + D&A (~2.6%) + SBC (0.9%). FY2026: guided ~16.1% adj op margin -> ~19.7%, less ~1.2pp Project Leap cash. From FY2027 a further ~0.5pp below the adjusted-margin-implied ~19.9% for recurring restructuring/'other' charges: Cognizant has booked a restructuring programme almost every year since 2019 (2019-20 Fit-for-Growth, 2022-24 NextGen, 2026 Leap), and without the haircut the build ran ~0.5pp of margin above its own FY2025 cash back-test and ~2pp above the FY2021-25 owner-FCF margin average (~9.8%, depressed by Sec.174-era cash taxes).

bull.narrative: Cognizant stays in the 'winner's circle': AI-builder positioning, $100M+ megadeals and 3Cloud/Astreya cross-sell lift organic growth to 5-6.5%, and the broader-shorter pyramid plus automation widen adjusted operating margin ~1.5pp toward 17.5-18% over the decade.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because GenAI substitution of billable hours is a live structural threat to the core revenue base, not a cyclical dip, and the share price's fall from $87 to $57 shows the market treats it as such. Base held at 50% because FY2026 is tracking guidance and bookings are strong. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs two independent things to go right, AI revenue outgrowing AI deflation AND sustained margin expansion against Indian-major pricing.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
